v: Understand the ways people sell online
Pick the model that suits your money and time
Own stock - you buy products, keep them at home or in a shop, and ship each order
Handmade - you make the product yourself: food, clothes, crafts, jewellery
Wholesale and resale - you buy in bulk from a market and sell single pieces with a margin
Selling for others - you list products of a supplier and take a commission; the supplier ships

b.v: A customer orders, you pack, a courier delivers. In Pakistan most buyers still pay cash on delivery (COD): the courier collects the cash and sends it to you a few days later, minus its charges. Online payment is growing, and it means fewer refused parcels.

v: A small starting stock - many people start with Rs 10,000 to 30,000
1 to 3 hours a day for messages, packing and posting
Patience: the first orders take weeks, not days

b.v: Be careful with anyone who sells you a 'ready-made shop' that 'earns by itself'. Every real shop needs work, good products and honest service.
Do this now:|Write which of the four models fits you.|Write how much money you can risk without hurting your home budget.|Write how many hours a day you can give.

v: Find a product people want
Check it is worth selling before you buy
Light and small - cheap to deliver
Hard to break - fewer returns
Something people buy again - tea, skin care, stationery, baby items
Priced between Rs 800 and Rs 5,000 - easy to buy, still leaves profit
Easy to explain in a photo

b.v: Step by step:|Search the product on XpertCreation Store and other shops.|Note how many sellers there are and their prices.|Read reviews: what do buyers complain about? That is your chance to do better.|Ask 10 people you know if they would buy it, and at what price.

v: Copies of famous brands - it is illegal and accounts get closed
Medicines, weapons, or anything that needs a licence you don't have
Products you cannot get again when they sell out

b.v: Do this now:|List 5 product ideas.|Score each from 1 to 5 for weight, breakage, repeat buying and profit.|Keep the top 2 for tomorrow.

day-3.t: Day 3 — Buying stock and setting the price

v: Find a reliable supplier
Work out your real cost and a fair price
Wholesale markets in your city
Factories and small makers who sell in bulk
Suppliers on business-to-business websites - order a sample first

b.v: Step by step:|Purchase price of one piece|+ packing (bag, box, tape, label)|+ your share of delivery, if you offer free delivery|+ a little for returns and damage (about 5%)|+ any platform or payment fee|= your real cost

Look at the market price, then make sure you keep a healthy profit over your real cost. Many small sellers aim for 25% to 40% profit. If the market price leaves you almost nothing, choose another product rather than selling at a loss.
Always buy a small quantity first. Check the quality yourself before buying 100 pieces.
Do this now:|Make a cost sheet for one product with the five lines above.|Write the price you will sell at and your profit per piece.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Photos and listings that sell

v: Take clear product photos with your phone
Write a title and description buyers trust
Daylight from a window, no harsh flash
Plain white or light background - a sheet of chart paper works
At least 4 photos: front, back, close-up, the product in use
Show the size: in a hand or next to a common object
Real photos of your own stock, never copied from others

b.v: What it is + key feature + size or quantity + who it is for. Example: 'Cotton baby blanket, soft double layer, 100 x 80 cm, for newborns'.

v: First line: the main benefit
Short points: material, size, colour, what is in the box
Care instructions and delivery time
Honest notes: if the colour looks slightly different in light, say so

b.v: Do this now:|Take 4 photos of one product.|Write its title with the formula.|Write a 5-point description.

day-5.t: Day 5 — Your shop on XpertCreation Store

v: Set up your shop
Add your first products with stock
Complete your XpertCreation profile with a real photo
Finish KYC - shops are approved only after it
Choose a shop name that is short and easy to say

b.v: Step by step:|Open Store and apply as a merchant.|Add your logo, banner, city and a short About text.|Write your delivery and return policy in plain words.|Pick a plan that fits the number of products you will list.

v: Upload the photos and listing from Day 4
Enter the quantity you really have
Set a reorder level - for example 5 - so you get a reminder before you run out
Use wholesale prices with a minimum quantity if you also sell to shops

b.v: Do this now:|Write your shop name and About text.|Add 3 products with photos, price and stock.

v: Handle an order from start to finish
Pack so nothing breaks

b.v: Step by step:|Confirm the order with the buyer by message or call, especially for cash on delivery.|Check the address and phone number.|Pack the same day if you can.|Book the courier and share the tracking number with the buyer.

v: A plastic bag inside a box keeps out water
Bubble wrap or newspaper around anything that can break
Label with name, address, phone and order number
A small thank-you card brings repeat buyers
Compare courier rates and how fast they pay you the COD cash
Decide: free delivery (price includes it) or a fixed delivery charge
Keep a list of parcels and follow up any that are late

b.v: Confirm cash-on-delivery orders before sending. Refused parcels cost you delivery both ways.
Do this now:|Write your order confirmation message.|Pack one product as if it were going to another city.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Returns, reviews and customer service

v: Write a fair return policy
Turn unhappy buyers into loyal ones
How many days the buyer has (for example 7 days)
Which items cannot be returned (used, opened food, undergarments)
Who pays the return delivery
How fast you refund or replace

b.v: Ask happy buyers to leave an honest review. Never write fake reviews or pay for them - buyers notice, and the platform can close your shop. One honest 4-star review with a photo is worth more than ten fake 5-star ones.

Step by step:|Reply within a few hours.|Say sorry for the trouble, even if it was the courier's fault.|Offer a solution: replace, refund or a discount on the next order.|Learn from it: change the packing, the photo or the description.
Do this now:|Write your return policy in 4 lines.|Write a polite reply to 'My item arrived broken'.

day-8.t: Day 8 — Big marketplaces and selling abroad

v: Understand how large international marketplaces work
Know what you need before you apply

b.v: Large marketplaces bring millions of buyers but charge a fee on every sale, and some charge a monthly fee. Many offer a warehouse service: you send your stock to their warehouse, and they pack, ship and handle returns for an extra fee.

v: Your ID card and proof of address
A bank account that can receive foreign payments
Sometimes a registered business and a tax number
Products with a barcode and proper labels
Money for stock, shipping to the warehouse and fees, before the first payment arrives
Learn with one or two products first
Work out every fee before you set the price
Expect a few months before steady sales
Handmade and local products (shawls, leather, ceramics) do well abroad

b.v: Many paid courses promise quick money from foreign marketplaces. Read each marketplace's own seller rules for free first; they change often.
Do this now:|List the documents you already have and the ones you would need.|Pick one local product that could sell abroad and write why.

v: Bring people to your shop
Turn first-time buyers into repeat buyers
Post your products on XpertConnect with a clear photo and price
Share your shop link with friends, family and local groups
Short videos: unboxing, how to use, before and after
Answer questions fast - quick replies win sales
Boost your best product, not your whole shop
Start with a small budget and check the results
Run an offer with an end date: 'Free delivery till Sunday'
A thank-you card with a small discount code
A message when new stock arrives
Bundles: buy 2, get a better price

b.v: Do this now:|Write 3 posts for one product: a photo post, a short video idea and an offer.|Write your thank-you card text.

v: Know if your shop is really making profit
Plan your next step
Every sale: date, product, price, delivery charge, COD received or not
Every expense: stock, packing, courier, boosts, fees
Once a month: total sales - total costs = profit

b.v: Cash on delivery money often reaches you days later, while you pay for new stock today. Keep some cash aside so you can restock without stopping.

v: Add products your buyers ask for
Drop products that sit unsold for months
When sales grow, register your business and get a tax number - it opens bigger buyers and marketplaces
Write down what you learned each month

b.v: Take the quiz to get your certificate. Then open one shop, list three good products, and serve your first ten buyers really well.
Do this now:|Make a one-month sheet for sales and expenses.|Write your goal for the next 3 months.
